title.narrative: Cocopallet Fast Forward; technical and commercial feasibility study to set up a production plant to produce pallets from coconut husk near the Asian equator

description.narrative: Coconut farmers are the poorest among farmers. Adding value to their activities, in particular by making use of their waste, has the potential to increase their incomes with 20-30% and have a positive impact on the environment. Countries like the Philippines harvest between 16 and 18 billion coconuts per year. More than 90% of the husks are wasted, which easily adds to 15,950,400 tonnes of waste per year that is usually burned and takes about 15-20 year to decompose in nature. Their burning and rotting leads to air pollution while it creates no value for anyone. CocoPallet International B.V. therefor has developed technologies to produce pallets made of Coconut husk. CocoPallet is 100% bio based, replaces single-use wooden pallets and prevents logging and transportation of millions of trees. Furthermore the product offers a sustainable and cheaper solution to other similar materials that are processed with chemicals which allows for circular recycling into other products, such as sustainable local building materials, packaging materials and charcoal, allowing farmers to earn extra income from a product that is considered waste. In order to prepare for future investments in the set-up of a production plant in South East Asia for the production of pallets from coconut husk, Technical Assistance (DGGF-TA) provided support to finalise a technical and commercial feasibility study and to develop a bankable business case to attract external investors. The project included the identification of local suppliers and production partners, selection of a location for the plant, a study into the uses of lignin of coconut fibres, the selection of 3 launching customers and the development of a project master schedule for the construction of the plant.The feasibility study has been successful and further investments in multiple production plants in the Philippines are currently being prepared. Each Cocopallet plant will be able to produce between 1.2 and 5 million CocoPallets, is expected to create approximately 200 new jobs, has the potential to help improve the livelihoods of at least 5,000 supplying coconut farmers and in turn will reduce the use of wood and the negative impact on the environment of coconut waste.
